## Findings

The dashboard's data model is task files (`<data-root>/<repo>/<slug>.yaml`), and those are only ever created by `worklog`'s three lifecycle hooks: `OnStart` (ticket promoted to `## Now`), `SyncEpicRoster` (epic child starts), and indirectly `OnDone`/`OnPR` (mutate an existing file). There is no code path that ever creates a task file for a ticket sitting in `## Next` or `## Someday` — by design, per `devboard/schema.md`'s ownership rule: a task file is "disposable live telemetry" for in-flight work (branch, session, phase, plan). `## Waiting` tickets are fine already — they were promoted through `## Now` first, so they already have a file from `OnStart`.

Separately, `worklog status --json` (`worklog/internal/cli/status.go`) already exposes exactly the data you'd want: Now/Waiting/Next/Someday as structured JSON with id, title, type, tags, repo, acceptance, etc., parsed from `WORK.md` by a small line-oriented parser (`worklog/internal/parse/work.go` — three regexes: section heading, `- [ ]` block start, `  - **Field**: value` metadata). But the devboard container doesn't ship the `worklog` binary — `server.py` already re-implements a second-source parser for `FEEDBACK.md` for this exact reason (documented in the README), reading straight off the read-only worklog mount that's already bind-mounted into the container for notes and `FEEDBACK.md`.

## Recommendation

Don't force Next/Someday tickets into the task-file schema — that would conflate "backlog" with "in-flight" and break invariants the rest of the UI leans on (phase-driven "in-flight" stat count, 2h stale-dimming, archive/un-archive semantics, per-repo directory grouping by task-file location). It would also require devboard-side bookkeeping to create/delete files as tickets move between Next/Someday/Now — duplicating state that `WORK.md` already owns, and violating the one-way worklog→devboard mirroring rule.

Instead, follow the precedent already set for `FEEDBACK.md`:

1. **Server**: add a small `WORK.md` parser to `server.py` (same regex shapes as `parse/work.go`), read from the already-mounted `WORKLOG_DIR`. Extract just `## Next` and `## Someday` blocks (id, title, type, repo, tags, acceptance) and add them to the `/api/tasks` payload, e.g. a `backlog: {next: [...], someday: [...]}` key alongside `repos`. Add `WORK.md` to `_snapshot()` so edits hot-reload over SSE like everything else. Missing/malformed `WORK.md` → empty backlog, never a page failure (same resilience contract as the Friction panel).
2. **Frontend**: render it as a new global collapsed band/fold, the same visual pattern as `Friction · N` — e.g. `Backlog · N`, split into Next/Someday, read-only (no phase bar, no plan meter, since none exists — just title/id/type badge/repo tag/acceptance snippet). No detail route, since there's no task-file detail to click into.
3. Keep the write boundary exactly as-is: the board stays fully read-only with respect to worklog state; promotion out of Next/Someday still only happens via `worklog start`, at which point the ticket naturally disappears from the backlog band and appears as a normal task card once `OnStart` writes its file.

This gets full backlog visibility with no new writer, no schema changes to task files, and no new failure modes — it's the same "second reader of the same format" pattern the codebase already uses for `FEEDBACK.md`.
